The draft remains subject to client review and agreement on disclosure schedules, indemnity limitations, and claims procedures. We suggest addressing those items together in the next turn.

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Subject to the disclosure schedules agreed by the parties and delivered at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the dates and periods stated therein.

4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations and claims procedures expressly agreed in this Agreement, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual losses incurred arising from liabilities of the Company existing at Closing that were not disclosed in this Agreement or the agreed disclosure schedules and that constitute a breach of the Seller's express representations or warranties. The Buyer shall not recover more than once for the same loss, including through any adjustment to the Purchase Price. Nothing in this clause limits liability for fraud. The parties shall agree before signing on the applicable indemnity cap, basket, survival periods, and claims procedures.

receiver.message_back: For Meridian, we require the financial statements to be prepared consistently under applicable accounting standards, with only specific, fairly disclosed schedule exceptions, and indemnification separately covering breaches of representations, warranties and covenants, pre-Closing taxes, and undisclosed liabilities existing at Closing, without requiring those liabilities also to breach an express representation. We propose a general cap equal to the Purchase Price, no basket, 24-month survival for general representations and survival through the applicable limitation period for fundamental representations and taxes, with fraud uncapped, timely notified claims preserved until resolved, and claims procedures that protect Buyer’s participation and settlement-consent rights; we accept the prohibition on double recovery.

drafter.private_reasoning: The draft appears to be on behalf of Seller. These edits offer a seller-side compromise without disclosing confidential information or accepting Buyer's proposed full-price general exposure. The independent undisclosed-liabilities indemnity materially expands Seller's risk and requires client approval before agreement. Referral interests should not influence that recommendation. All proposed terms are visible in the operative text.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: For Seller, we propose the attached compromise, subject to client approval. We have incorporated consistent accounting standards, specific schedule exceptions, separate indemnity categories, and independent coverage for undisclosed Closing liabilities. In exchange, we propose a 25% general cap, a 0.5% deductible basket, and 18-month general survival, with separate treatment for fundamental representations, taxes, and fraud. The revised procedures preserve timely claims and protect Buyer's participation and settlement-consent rights while retaining reasonable defense controls and the prohibition on double recovery.

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with applicable accounting standards consistently applied throughout the periods presented and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the dates and periods stated therein, except as specifically and fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules agreed by the parties and delivered at signing. Each exception must identify the representation qualified and describe its nature and scope in sufficient detail to permit the Buyer reasonably to understand it. The Seller further represents that it has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, that this Agreement is binding on it, and that it owns the Shares free of liens and has authority to transfer them. These latter representations, together with any expressly agreed representations concerning the Company's organization and capitalization, are the Fundamental Representations.
edits.name: Financial statements and fundamental representations

edits.text:
4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual losses incurred arising from (a) any breach of the Seller's representations or warranties; (b) any breach of the Seller's covenants; (c) taxes of the Company attributable to periods ending on or before Closing and the portion through Closing of any period spanning Closing; and (d) liabilities of the Company existing at Closing that were not specifically and fairly disclosed in this Agreement or the agreed disclosure schedules. Recovery under paragraph (d) does not require a breach of an express representation or warranty. Taxes for a period spanning Closing shall be allocated using a closing-of-the-books method, except that periodic taxes shall be allocated by days.

Except for claims involving Fundamental Representations, taxes, or fraud, the Seller's aggregate liability under this clause shall not exceed 25% of the Purchase Price. Claims under paragraphs (a), other than for Fundamental Representations, and (d) shall be recoverable only to the extent their aggregate amount exceeds 0.5% of the Purchase Price. Claims for Fundamental Representations and taxes shall not be subject to that basket, and total liability under this clause, including amounts paid under the general cap, shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except for fraud, which shall be uncapped and not subject to any contractual basket or survival limitation.

General representations and claims under paragraph (d) shall survive for 18 months after Closing. Fundamental Representations and tax claims shall survive through the applicable limitation period. Covenants shall survive through their stated performance periods and the applicable limitation period for claims concerning their breach. A claim notified in writing before the applicable survival period expires shall survive until finally resolved. Notice shall describe the factual basis and estimated amount, to the extent reasonably known; inability to quantify a claim shall not invalidate otherwise sufficient notice.

The Buyer shall give reasonably prompt written notice of third-party claims. Delay shall reduce recovery only to the extent the Seller is materially prejudiced, subject to the survival deadlines above. The Seller may assume the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Buyer upon acknowledging its indemnity obligation, subject to the agreed limitations. The Buyer may participate with its own counsel at its own expense, except that reasonable separate-counsel costs shall be indemnifiable where an actual conflict requires separate representation. The Buyer may control the defense where the claim involves criminal proceedings, material nonmonetary relief against the Buyer or Company, or reasonably anticipated exposure exceeding the remaining applicable cap. Neither party may settle a claim for which indemnity is sought without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The Buyer need not consent to any settlement that lacks an unconditional release of the Buyer and Company, requires an admission of wrongdoing by either, or imposes nonmonetary obligations on either. The parties shall reasonably cooperate in the defense, without requiring waiver of privilege.

The Buyer shall not recover more than once for the same loss, including through any adjustment to the Purchase Price. Nothing in this clause limits liability for fraud.
edits.name: Indemnity compromise
